content.rationale: Cutting a release is one local step: `scripts/release.py`. It takes the named version from its caller (an argument, `--version`, `--tag v<v>`, a bare `v<v>`, `VERSION` in the environment, or stdin), reads the token the version decision records (nlomlqum: `0.0.0-dev`), and puts the named version in the manifest's `[package] version` in its place. The token comes from the record and nowhere else, so the substitution follows the graph rather than a literal: a different token in nlomlqum is the token that gets replaced. The substitution is a substitution and not an overwrite: it applies only when the manifest carries the recorded token, or as a no-op when it already carries the requested version, and a manifest carrying any other version is refused — non-zero exit, a named reason, nothing written, no `dist` or `cargo` invocation — because a tree at a version the record does not carry has already been released or was never in the token state, and the release step is not the place to decide which; the releaser reruns with the version the manifest already carries or restores the token. If nlomlqum is absent the release is refused for the same reason: there is no recorded token to substitute, and the script does not fall back to a literal. The substitution happens first because dist derives the tag it releases from the manifest version and refuses a manifest that disagrees with the tag; the releaser commits the substituted manifest and the refreshed lockfile, then pushes the tag. After the substitution the script drives the release from `dist-workspace.toml` with `dist build`, `dist host` (create, upload, release) and `cargo publish`, and stops on the first step that fails. The dist config stays the single description of the release: the same four targets (aarch64 and x86_64 macOS, aarch64 and x86_64 Linux gnu), the same shell and Homebrew installers, GitHub hosting. The script reads that file and never rewrites it — it runs no `dist init` and generates nothing — so the plan and the machinery cannot drift from each other. What is gone is the generated workflow set under `.github/workflows/` (release and publish workflows); the script replaces them as the release machinery rather than being called by them. The consequence is accepted and stated plainly: the repository now has no CI at all, no pull-request checks and no tag-triggered release, and nothing in CI invokes this script. A release is a human running the script from a local checkout, so it is reproducible only as far as that person's toolchain is: `dist build` builds what the machine it runs on can build, so shipping all four platforms' binaries per release needs the cross toolchains on that machine, where the removed workflows used a build matrix of four runners and nothing replaces that matrix; the platforms and installers are still the dist config's, not this script's, choice. The manifest it edits is I1a's (trolstmt) and the token it replaces is the version decision's (nlomlqum); this node decides only how a release is driven.
